title: Multi-statement writes that require atomicity are issued through the batch surface; the facade never surfaces a partial-batch result
description: When the facade needs to commit two or more statements as one unit (a domain operation that writes to more than one table, an insert-then-update pair whose semantics depend on both landing), the facade issues them through `db.batch([<prepared statements>])`. On any statement in the batch failing, the facade surfaces the failure to the caller without surfacing any of the batch's other statement results as though they had committed. Single-statement writes commit as their own transaction; the facade does not synthesise atomicity across independent facade calls, and consumers do not chain facade calls under the assumption that they run in one transaction.
rationale: D1 does not expose explicit BEGIN/COMMIT to the Worker binding; `batch()` is the only vendor-supported multi-statement atomicity primitive, and its contract is that a mid-batch failure rolls back the sequence. Naming that surface explicitly at the REQ level puts every domain operation whose correctness depends on multi-statement atomicity on the one path the vendor's contract supports. Refusing to expose partial-batch results means a consumer never has to reason about whether an error is 'some statements landed, some did not'; either the batch committed or it did not.
